standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the factorisation j : X -> T followed by a finite pi, the criterion that a quasi-compact open immersion is closed as soon as specializations lift along it, the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part over an elementary etale neighbourhood of the base, and the lifting of specializations along the resulting etale morphism.

core_obligations: Reduce to a quasi-finite separated morphism with support equal to X: let Z be the scheme theoretic support of F, note that Z -> S is separated of finite type with finite fibres and hence separated and quasi-finite, and use the supported on closed lemma to replace X by Z and F by the induced module (proof lines 5061-5072).

Dispose of the easy implications: a finite morphism is proper and a proper morphism is pure relative to its base, so (2) implies (3), while (3) implies (1) trivially; it remains to show that (1) implies (2) (proof lines 5074-5079).

Show that the quasi-compact open immersion is closed: assume S affine, use the factorisation through a finite morphism to write f as pi composed with a quasi-compact open immersion j, and prove j is closed by lifting specializations; for a specialization t' leading to t with t' = j(x), use the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part over an elementary etale neighbourhood of the base to find an open and closed piece V finite over U with a unique point over u, lift the specialization to a point v' of V mapping to t', observe that v' is a relative associated point because the fibre over u' is a finite discrete set equal to the support, and use purity of F relative to S to conclude that v' specializes into the fibre over u, hence that the unique point of V over u lies in X and so t lies in X (proof lines 5080-5120).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the scheme theoretic support, which is quasi-finite and separated over the base (proof lines 5061-5072).
Note that finiteness implies universal purity and purity trivially implies purity (proof lines 5074-5079).
Assume purity and show the factorisation open immersion is closed by lifting specializations along the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part (proof lines 5080-5120).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a separated finite type morphism whose module has finite support in every fibre, purity relative to the base, finiteness of the scheme theoretic support over the base and universal purity are equivalent (statement lines 5046-5059, tag 05K4). The proof reduces to the case where the support is all of X, then has to show that two easy implications plus one substantial one hold: assuming purity, the quasi-finite separated morphism is factored through a finite morphism and a quasi-compact open immersion, and the immersion is shown to be closed by lifting an arbitrary specialization using the etale splitting of the quasi-finite part, the identification of the lifted point as a relative associated point, and purity itself. That specialization lifting is the substance, so the claim is H2.
